_comment: Executable claims for OPEN-DECISIONS.md, one JSON object per line. `status` is the state of THIS CLAIM, not of the whole OD entry — an entry can be partly resolved (OD-56's Python half is fixed while its Node transitives are not, so its aiohttp/cryptography claim is `resolved` while OD-56 itself stays open). resolved = the claim MUST hold; if it stops holding, the fix regressed. open = the claim must NOT hold yet; if it starts holding, strike that part of the entry off. See scripts/check_decision_claims.sh and CLAUDE.md §5b.

claim: analytics.controller.ts is guarded (no longer an unauthenticated paid-LLM surface)
verify: grep -q '@UseGuards' apps/api-gateway/src/analytics/analytics.controller.ts

claim: jwt-secret.ts throws rather than falling back to a published string
verify: grep -q 'throw new Error' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/jwt-secret.ts

claim: SimposController is guarded AND SimposModule stays gated out of production
verify: grep -q 'UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)' apps/api-gateway/src/simpos/simpos.controller.ts && grep -q 'NODE_ENV !== "production" ? \[SimposModule\]' apps/api-gateway/src/app.module.ts

claim: no bare fetch() of a user-supplied URL remains in vendor-page-extractor — both sites go through safeFetch
verify: test "$(grep -c 'await fetch(' apps/api-gateway/src/vendor-intel/vendor-page-extractor.service.ts)" = 0 && test "$(grep -c 'safeFetch(' apps/api-gateway/src/vendor-intel/vendor-page-extractor.service.ts)" = 2

claim: splitPdfIfLarge caps pages, so chunk count cannot track an uploaded PDF's page count
verify: grep -q 'MAX_PAGES' apps/api-gateway/src/menus/parsers/scan-parser.service.ts && grep -q 'effectivePages' apps/api-gateway/src/menus/parsers/scan-parser.service.ts

claim: the four pos_* tables carry foreign keys (was 3, now 13)
verify: test "$(grep -c 'foreign key' supabase/migrations/20260825140000_pos_referential_integrity.sql)" -ge 10

claim: aiohttp and cryptography are pinned at or above their patched versions (the Python half of OD-56; the Node transitives are separate and still open)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/requirements.txt').read(); a=re.search(r'^aiohttp==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); c=re.search(r'^cryptography==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); v=lambda x:[int(n) for n in x.split('.')]; sys.exit(0 if v(a)>=[3,14,3] and v(c)>=[50,0,0] else 1)"

claim: calendar_agent's regex fallback is NOT fed the prompt template (fixed in #57; the separate question of provider_important_dates not existing in production is OD-68)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/agents/calendar_agent.py').read(); sys.exit(1 if re.search(r'_regex_date_extraction\\(\\s*prompt\\s*\\)', s) else 0)"

claim: no file in apps/web/src imports the browser anon-key Supabase client any more (OD-45 removed useReportQueries; useSommelierQueries is the last one). Holds when the sommelier surface is routed through the gateway, or when the hook is deleted
verify: test "$(grep -rl 'lib/supabase' apps/web/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' | grep -v 'src/lib/supabase.ts' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 0

claim: a migration revokes anon's DML on the procurement document tables, so the invoice store is not readable/writable with the public anon key
verify: python3 -c "import glob,re,sys; pat=re.compile(r'revoke\s+all[^;]*\bprocurement_documents\b[^;]*\bfrom\b[^;]*\banon\b',re.I|re.S); sys.exit(0 if [f for f in glob.glob('supabase/migrations/*.sql') if pat.search(open(f,errors='ignore').read())] else 1)"

verify: grep -q 'alter default privileges' supabase/migrations/20260825210000_od72_revoke_client_grants.sql && grep -q 'OD-72 not closed' supabase/migrations/20260825210000_od72_revoke_client_grants.sql

The CLASS is held by scripts/check_definer_functions_closed.py, the end-state check: schema-parity.yml runs it as the step right after `supabase db reset --no-seed` -- first a canary with the allowlist emptied, which must report supabase_functions.http_request() (the local stack's platform webhook, SECURITY DEFINER and granted to anon/authenticated by the pinned CLI), then the real run, whose `DEFINER-CHECK OK -- <k> in public` line is asserted with k >= 7 (MIN_PUBLIC_SECDEF = 7) -- and a --self-test step that asserts at least 61 cases run [CORRECTED 2026-09-19, PR #391 audit, Notes to close: stale prose, never updated as the brackets below raised this floor -- it now asserts at least 576 cases run, the value in force per this row's own verify]. It fails when any SECURITY DEFINER function outside the system schemas and outside extensions answers to PUBLIC, anon or authenticated (by the built-in default, a grant, ownership or role membership) unless CLIENT_CALLABLE excuses it with an ADR. This row pins those two steps, their position and their floors statically, and runs the self-test. Arm (c) of scripts/check_new_tables_are_locked_down.py is a fast pre-check for common spellings, not the authority; this row also pins its ci.yml steps and its report (arm-(c) OK tally, self-test at least 89 cases) [CORRECTED 2026-09-19, PR #391 audit, Notes to close: stale prose -- arm (c)'s self-test floor is now 95, the value in force per this row's own verify]. ~~The CLASS is held by arm (c) of scripts/check_new_tables_are_locked_down.py, a CI step with its own --self-test step [...]: [...] none may be client-executable when the corpus finishes [...]~~ [CORRECTED 2026-09-18, round 5, source: PR #391 verifier round 4: a lexical arm cannot hold the class. Four review rounds each found spellings that re-open a definer while arm (c) exits 0 (a single-quoted DO body, `to group anon`, a grant to a role anon is a member of, a revoke under `if false` or undone by a savepoint, dynamic EXECUTE shapes, rename-then-grant, overloads). Replayed as migrations on a full-corpus build, the end-state check exits 1 on every one that leaks; see ADR 0159. Arm (c)'s three rules stand as a pre-check: same-file revoke, the end state as its replay of the text models it, and the per-schema no-op refused.] [Added 2026-09-18, round 4, source: PR #391 verifier round 3: arm (c) reads static migration text. Dynamic SQL (a variable, `||`, concat(), a later format() argument, `execute (...)`) is out of its reach except the EXECUTEd-literal shapes its --self-test names; see ADR 0159 Decision, residuals.] [CORRECTED 2026-09-18, source: PR #391 audit: the 2026-09-17 row certified that no-op as the class fix by grepping for its text. See ADR 0159.] This row pins the repo, not production: read 2026-09-18, production has not applied 20260917010400 and increment_trust_counter is still =X/postgres there. [Added 2026-09-18, source: PR #391 verifier: the verify trusted only the guard's exit codes, so the guard gutted to exit 0 (at its entry point, at the top of main(), or at the top of run_self_test()) left it green. It now asserts what the guard prints: the arm-(c) OK line with at least 7 SECURITY DEFINER creates on the real tree, and SELF-TEST OK with at least 89 cases run; the floor was 32 until the round-2 verifier's bypass shapes added ten self-test cases, and 42 until round 4 pinned every arm-(c) rule (47 more cases).] [2026-09-18, round 6, source: PR #391 verifier round 5: the allowlist matched on signature alone, so dropping supabase_functions.http_request() and recreating it as a callable definer granted to anon passed (A1c); a role granted to authenticator was not judged (A8); and this row stayed green under `if: false` on the self-test step (M1) and a neutered canary condition (M2). The end-state check now judges PUBLIC plus every role authenticator is a member of (service_role excepted, with its reason), and excuses an allowlisted function only while its identity matches the pin (owner, language, return type, returns-set, kind, proconfig, md5(prosrc) cb8a5741f829fe414ecd51c25be75c9a, measured from the v2.116.0 template); arm (c) refuses any migration naming supabase_functions (exit 2). This row now pins the canary's three lines verbatim and adjacent, the self-test step's `if:` exactly, the pinned owner and md5 in the script, arm (c)'s narrowed OK line, and floors of 105 (end-state self-test) and 95 (arm (c) self-test).] [2026-09-19, round 7, source: the founder's call on round 6's named residuals -- "do what the optimal scenario would do, no we can do this later or second plan": the end-state check now also fails on a SECURITY DEFINER function PostgreSQL runs for a judged role with no EXECUTE check against it (ADR 0159, REACH THROUGH ANOTHER OBJECT): a trigger on any write a judged role can make land on its table (directly, through a column privilege, an auto-updatable view, a rule, a partition or inheritance child, or a foreign-key CASCADE/SET NULL/SET DEFAULT action as the table's owner), everything else a cascaded table's objects call, index and statistics expressions under autoanalyze or MAINTAIN, a materialized view's query under REFRESH, the eight support functions of an aggregate a judged role may EXECUTE, a function taking or returning a type a judged role owns, and -- as PUBLIC -- every function the catalog wires into operator families, estimators, planner support, types, ranges, casts, event triggers, text search, languages, foreign-data wrappers, access methods, conversions, transforms and TABLESAMPLE. PR #391 verifier rows A3 and A9 (and the round-6 verifier's N1) now exit 1. This row now greps the trigger arm, the aggregate arm and the classifier's reach-through merge in the script, and asserts a self-test floor of 342 (was 105) in the step and in its own run.] [2026-09-19, round-7 repair, source: the round-7 verifier (NOT READY: no adversarial pass, no number re-run, and an open question that the reach query followed only an object's direct pg_depend rows to pg_proc). Measured on PGlite: 23 of 44 adversarial plants ran a closed definer as an object's owner for anon while the round-7 check exited 0 -- an operator, a domain cast, a SQL-standard body, a policy's subquery or a whole-row reference in an owner-context object, a row an UPDATE moves between partitions, a view over a view with INSTEAD OF triggers, PL/pgSQL or a builtin that runs SQL text in owner context, and functions, types or relations a judged role owns. The end-state check now walks what every owner-context object names and exits 1 on a definer it reaches, 2 (BLIND) on owner-context code the catalog does not describe; all 44 plants give the wanted exit and every control exits 0 (ADR 0159, round-7 repair). Each query is now pinned by the md5 of its exact text (QUERIES_MD5), since the repair's mutation table showed a clause pin cannot see a falsifier added beside it. This row now also greps the walk's dependency edge, the opaque-body BLIND rule, the walk's rows in the verdict, the exit-2 wiring of BLIND, the md5 comparison and REACH_SQL's pinned md5 (7b2f0774372a11aeaff6cb518075f64b, the text the repair's replay measured), and asserts a self-test floor of 491 (was 342) in the step and in its own run.] [2026-09-19, round-7 repair 2, source: the round-7 verifier's re-run (NOT READY: no adversarial pass, no number re-measured, and an open question that owner-context paths reach a function through catalog objects the walk does not follow). The check now seeds column statistics and foreign-key checks, follows negators and commutators, adds the five type-by-OID builtins and satisfies_hash_partition to the BLIND list, judges the estimator path as PUBLIC, and walks once per seed object (the storage-api proxy: 97.5 s to 3.0 s on PGlite). All 27 plants give the wanted exit and every control exits 0. This row now also greps the estimator arm, the column-statistics seed, the foreign-key-check seed and the per-seed-object walk, pins REACH_SQL's new md5 (6d61c09d09ad23185b7c69545bbb15eb) and asserts a self-test floor of 576 (was 491) in the step and in its own run.]

Subject and display names become =?UTF-8?B?...?= words split on whole characters, every line at most 76 characters, with CR/LF and other control characters collapsed to one space. Addresses are trimmed, then refused on an interior control character. A named entry (ending in <addr>) must hold exactly one mailbox: a quoted name that is not one quoted-string ("A" <a@x>, "B" <b@x>) or an unquoted name containing <, >, @ or , (A <a@x>, B <b@x>; a@x, B <b@x>) is refused, never collapsed; a bare a@x, b@y list is written as before. Our own Message-ID is refused on a control character. A refusal returns success:false with refusal {kind:'header'} and Gmail is never called; sendProviderEmail throws SendRefusedBeforeSendError and isDefiniteSendRefusal recognises it by instanceof, never by text (the text embeds the vendor's address), so the draft is released and the error names the header, not GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN. The vendor's In-Reply-To/References are REBUILT from their <msg-id> tokens (threadingHeader; an id too long for a 998-character line is dropped), never refused: RFC 5322 folding (CRLF+TAB) in stored vendor values used to make every reply on that thread fail. claim: Membership only (ADR 0164, the founder 2026-09-18: 'Membership only'; v3.0-TECH-DEBT 44.1r, closed). A session is in a house only while the person holds an active user_restaurant_access row there. AuthService.generateTokens is the only minter (the gateway's only two jwtService.sign calls are inside it) and names the house it is given only where such a row exists, with that row's role, else no house and a null role; its callers (signIn, refresh, switch, register, join, verify-email, and since 2026-09-25 ADR 0213's registerAccount and registerAccountWithGoogle, which name no house, and createFirstHouse, which names the house it just wrote a membership row for) are pinned by their exact argument lists. refreshAccessToken keeps a member's house and, for a person no longer a member, returns a pair naming no house plus houseAccessEnded (never moving them); a bad refresh token is 401, a failed read 503. validateJwtPayload refuses a token naming a house with no active row: 401 code HOUSE_ACCESS_ENDED with the house. switchRestaurant has no organisation fallback: it mints through generateTokens and refuses a non-member (403 NOT_A_MEMBER). getBranchesForUser lists active memberships only (no organisation read, no users-row read). Before: refresh carried payload.restaurantId ?? users.restaurant_id forward unchecked, the strategy admitted a token whose house gave no role, and the fallback opened 7 person-house pairs (all simulation accounts; it served 2 sessions, 2026-09-03). sessions-follow-membership.spec.ts pins the behaviour at runtime. Static verify, comment-stripped and whitespace-normalised: pins generateTokens' membership block, payload and return, the sign sites, the call list, refreshAccessToken and switchRestaurant whole, the refusal, the branches read, and the spec titles. Mutation-tested 2026-09-18: 11 mutants red (S1-S11: the membership check bypassed or pre-filled, the ended-house branch or the switch refusal made unreachable, refresh falling back to users.restaurant_id, a second sign site, a join minting the users row's house, the organisation read restored in branches, the refusal's code changed, the users read error ignored, the branches is_active filter dropped), 1 comment-and-blank-line control green. [Updated 2026-09-26, PR #477 merge (ADR 0225): refreshAccessToken now also refuses a token from a session a password change ended, before the house check runs; this row's pinned function text includes that check, and the membership invariant this row guards is unchanged.] [Amended 2026-09-26, PR #479 (ADR 0229): generateTokens gained a fourth argument, authTime, threaded through every caller listed above plus a new one, issueSessionForVerifiedSignIn (the passkey/emailed-code sign-in door); the membership check and the call list's house arguments are unchanged.] [Amended 2026-09-27, ADR 0090 audit fix (commit b88c27053, PR #479): issueSessionForVerifiedSignIn no longer mints directly -- it routes through this.signIn(signedIn, false, lastHouses, signedInNow()), the same path a password sign-in uses.] [2026-09-27, PR #479 merge of main (#477): the two branches each amended this row; merged into one row (a duplicate id fails the guard). The pinned call list and refreshAccessToken text are re-pinned to the merged code: refresh carries both #477's session-version refusal and #479's auth_time; changePassword's kept-session mint (#477) now also carries the session's auth_time unchanged (a password change is not a sign-in). House arguments unchanged.] [Amended 2026-09-27, PR #479, ADR 0229 fork 10 (the founder, item 78, "Refresh refuses lapsed (Recommended)"): refreshAccessToken now also refuses, with SESSION_ENDED and before any token is signed, an account whose unproven password has lapsed (holdsUnprovenPassword and unprovenPasswordHasLapsed), except a dev-bypass session where dev bypass is on; the pinned text is re-pinned to it. The membership invariant this row guards is unchanged.] [Amended 2026-09-28, PR #479, ADR 0229 forks 11-13 (the founder, round 15, items 81-83): verifyEmail now needs a session of the link's own account (fork 12) and names that session's house, else the users row's (sessionHouse ?? user.restaurant_id ?? null), still through generateTokens' membership check; joinViaInvite mints a pair naming no house when the membership is held (fork 13; generateTokens(user, false, null, signedInNow())). The pinned call list is re-pinned to both. The membership invariant is unchanged.]

A session in no house has no house and no role, and reaches almost nothing (ADR 0164, R4; the founder: users.role 'stops mattering'; v3.0-TECH-DEBT 44.1t, closed). JwtStrategy.validate sets restaurantId to the token's house only and role to the house role or null, reading neither users.role nor users.restaurant_id. JwtAuthGuard, after the email check, calls assertHouseChosen, which refuses 403 HOUSE_REQUIRED for a session with no house on any route not marked @AllowsNoHouse(); exactly 15 routes are marked (14 in AuthController, the 14th being POST /auth/register/house since 2026-09-25 so an ADR 0213 account-only signup can open its first house, and GET /organizations/branches, listed in no-house-session.spec.ts). assertTenantMatch lets a tenantless session name a house only in the BODY of the one @AllowsTenantChange route (choosing a house), never in a path or query. GET /auth/me reports the session's house and its role there, null for both in no house, never users.role. Before: a token naming no house acted in the users row's house at users.role, which after PR #393 is how a leaver's next login carried the role their old house gave them. Static verify: pins the strategy lines, the guard's order and metadata read, assertHouseChosen whole, the marker count, the tenantless branch, the /auth/me lines, and the spec titles. Mutation-tested 2026-09-18: 7 mutants red (N1-N7: the house check commented out or made unreachable, a 15th route marked (now: a 16th), the tenantless exemption widened to every route, /auth/me falling back to users.role, the email check changed, the switch route's marker removed), 1 comment-only control green. [Amended 2026-09-28, PR #479, ADR 0229 forks 11-13 (the founder, round 15, items 81-83): two more routes are marked @AllowsNoHouse, 17 in all: POST /auth/verify-email (fork 12: the link now needs a session, which may be in no house) and POST /auth/held-memberships/accept (fork 13: a held joiner's session names no house). Neither names a house in its body; no-house-session.spec.ts lists both.]

The sign-in rule (ADR 0164, R1-R3; the founder 2026-09-18/19: 'if they own couple houses ... we let them choose which', 'after quite some time let them choose which restaurant to go'): 0 active memberships, no house and no role; 1, that house; 2 or more, the house this device used last if it is still theirs and was used within HOUSE_RETURN_WINDOW_MS (7 days, defined exactly once in apps/, its own constant), otherwise a pair naming no house plus chooseHouse with the houses. Password, dev-bypass, Google and Microsoft sign-in all return this.signIn(...), which reads memberships, takes the authenticated person's newest lastHouses hint and applies signInHouse. The web sends lastHouses — since item 8 (2026-09-19), only the hint for the email being submitted, via lastHouseHintFor, never every account the device remembers — on all three sign-in calls, takes the active house from the TOKEN (never branches[0]), no longer relabels on a refused switch ('proceeding with X-Restaurant-Id header only' is gone), sends a session in no house to /choose-house (routed in App.tsx and vercel.json); the phone sends — since the round-3 parity fix, 2026-09-19, only the hint for the email being signed in, via hintFor, mirroring the web's lastHouseHintFor — and routes a session in no house to its chooser. [Amended 2026-09-26, PR #479 (ADR 0229): signIn and every sign-in return now carry a fourth argument, authTime (signedInNow() from each of these four interactive doors) -- the house-choosing logic itself is unchanged.] Static verify: pins the window definition and its uniqueness, signInHouse and signIn whole, the four sign-in returns, and the web and mobile wiring.
